body.statement: There is a universal constant \(C_\beta<\infty\) such that every admissible sequence satisfies \[\Pr\!\left\{\beta(G_n)\le C_\beta\frac{n\log(d_n+1)}{d_n^2}\right\}\longrightarrow1.\] The proof must be uniform over sequences that cross the sparse and coupling regimes. Below a sufficiently large universal multiple of \(\log n\), a degree-preserving switching enumeration directly under the uniform simple regular law must give the required \(o(1)\) failure probability, without conditioning a configuration model on simplicity. At and above that threshold, a contained binomial graph from the Kim--Vu sandwich transfers the decreasing balanced-hole event.
body.justification: This theorem identifies the logarithmic balanced-hole scale by a uniform-simple switching argument below the verified sandwich threshold and monotone coupling above it.
body.gap: CooperEtAl2002RandomRegular characterizes ordinary one-color independence, whereas this signed closed-neighborhood packing excludes only opposite-arm centers at graph distance at most two.
body.consumer: Combined with Proposition 1, it rules out every design-estimator pair below order \(d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\).
